sections.html:
Clearfield County deeds are recorded at the Register and Recorder's Office, on the first level of the courthouse. The phone is 814-765-2641, extension 5012. Six public workstations there let you look up documents filed in the office.

The Recorder of Deeds division takes anything tied to real estate, plus notary public bonds and commissions, UCC filings and military discharges. It also issues copies and certified copies.

For a seller, this office is the last stop. Once the deed is signed at closing, it goes here, and recording puts the new owner's title on the public record.

Every deed must be taken to the county's Uniform Parcel Identifier office for a UPI stamp before the recorder will accept it. The fee is $10 per parcel. Questions go to 814-765-2641, extension 2042. Deeds can be pre-approved for the UPI before the day of recording.

Sellers often assume recording is a single stop. It is two. A title agent usually sends the deed to the UPI office a day or two early, gets the stamp back, then delivers the stamped deed to the recorder with the fee and the tax payments. If you are closing without a title company, ask the county how pre-approval works before you set a closing date.

The recorder's own deed checklist says the same thing: no UPI stamp from the Assessment Office, no recording.

A deed or a mortgage is $79.75. Names over four cost 50 cents each, and each page over four adds $2. Where no fee is listed, the Recorder of Deeds sets one.

The posted schedule carries an effective date of March 27, 2020, so call the office for the exact total before closing. Recording fees and transfer taxes are due when the document is recorded. Make checks payable to the Recorder of Deeds office.

sections.h2: When a Statement of Value is needed
sections.html:
Expect to file a Statement of Value if the deed leaves out the full price, if the house changes hands as a gift, if you claim a tax exemption, or if it was bought at a tax claim sale or sheriff's sale. Real estate that passes through an estate by will also needs one. File it signed and dated.

The one exception is a transfer exempt only because the parties are close family: grandparent, parent, child, brother or sister.

Pennsylvania's realty transfer tax is 1 percent at the state level, collected at the recorder's window, often alongside a local tax. Both buyer and seller answer for it. Some family transfers, property passing by will or intestacy, and farms are exempt.

  • The deed carries the buyer's signed certificate of address.
  • It names the municipality and county where the property sits.
  • Land that crosses municipal or school district lines needs the percentage in each, so the local tax is split properly.
  • The acknowledgment date cannot be earlier than the date on the document.

Two search products are open to the public. Landex Remote is the full tool, with the same search criteria as the software in the courthouse, and it suits someone who searches often. Landex Webstore is the basic version for occasional use. It can search several counties at once and narrow results by county, instrument type and municipality. Viewing images requires a credit card payment. For help with the online products, call 717-274-5890.

Before you list, pull your last recorded deed, any open mortgage, and any easement or right of way. A buyer's title search will find all of these, and it is better to learn about a problem now than at the closing table. If an old mortgage was paid off but never released on record, ask your lender for the satisfaction piece.

A document with a faulty acknowledgment gets sent back. Faulty means missing the county, state, date, the name of the person or corporate officer appearing, or the notary's signature, seal or expiration date. The office will not take blanket assignments, releases or satisfactions.

  • Re-recorded or corrective documents must state the reason and carry a new acknowledgment.
  • Several documents from one transaction must be numbered in the order they should be recorded.
  • Foreign language documents need a written English translation.
  • Every package needs a return envelope, stamped and addressed, big enough for the document.

For electronic recording, the vendors are Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and CSC at 866-652-0111. A title company already set up with either one can skip the courier. The county also runs a free Landex Record Alert program that sends an email or text if someone tries to record a deed under your name or parcel number. To sign up, use the parcel number printed under Map # on your tax invoice.

The county's population was estimated at 78,100 in July 2025, down 3.1 percent from the 2020 base. There were 38,429 housing units, and owners occupy 78.5 percent of occupied homes. Median owned-home value is $137,000, median monthly gross rent is $791, and median household income is $62,152. DuBois is the largest city and Clearfield borough is the county seat.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller at the recorder
sections.html:
In practice the sequence runs like this. The deed is signed and notarized at closing. The title agent or attorney gets the UPI stamp, adds the buyer's certificate of address, and prepares checks for the recording fee and the transfer tax. The package then goes to the recorder by courier, by mail with a return envelope, or electronically through one of the two vendors above.

If you are handling a sale yourself, bring or send the original signed deed, the UPI stamp, a Statement of Value if one applies, and checks written to the Recorder of Deeds. Call 814-765-2641, extension 5012 first and ask what the current total will be for your page count.

A cash buyer who closes quickly still has to go through the same two stops, the UPI office and the recorder, so build those into the timeline.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for a Clearfield County deed?
faqs.a: A deed or mortgage is $79.75, plus 50 cents for each name over four and $2 for each page over four. The schedule dates from March 27, 2020, so confirm the total with the office at 814-765-2641, extension 5012.

faqs.q: What is the UPI fee in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: It is $10 per parcel, and the stamp must be on a deed before the recorder will accept it. Call 814-765-2641, extension 2042 to ask about pre-approval.

faqs.q: Is e-recording offered in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile (800-460-5657) and CSC (866-652-0111) handle e-recording deeds. Contact one of them to start.

faqs.q: When is a Statement of Value required in Clearfield County?
faqs.a: It is required when the deed does not state full consideration, when the transfer is a gift, when an exemption is claimed, for tax claim and sheriff sales, and when property passes by will. A transfer exempt only because of a family relationship does not need one.

faqs.q: Who pays Pennsylvania realty transfer tax?
faqs.a: The 1 percent state tax is a joint liability of buyer and seller. Check the sales contract for how the cost is split. The tax is collected at the recording window.
